title: Giudicato of Cagliari
capsule: The Giudicato (Judicate) of Cagliari was one of four autonomous kingdoms into which Sardinia fragmented after Byzantine imperial authority collapsed during the Arab expansion of the 8th–9th centuries, occupying the island's entire southern zone across thirteen administrative subdivisions called curatoriae. The capital shifted inland from the exposed coastal city to Santa Igia, protected by marshland. Constantine I, ruling around 1089, bore the title rex et iudex Caralitanus and maintained close ties with both Pisa and the papacy, emblematic of the judicates' careful navigation between Italian commercial powers and the universal church. The kingdom ended in 1258 when Judge John's attempt to break Pisan dominance by allying with Genoa led to his assassination; a Pisan-led coalition then besieged and destroyed Santa Igia, partitioning Cagliari's territory among the Della Gherardesca family, the Judicate of Arborea, and Gallura.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The curatoriae administrative divisions are attested in medieval Sardinian documents (condaghi), giving reasonable detail on internal boundaries; outer limits relative to neighboring judicates are less precisely defined.
